newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $67, passed - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle bid $67, passed - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle early Thursday were lightly bid at $67.00 per cwt, but the bids were passed by owners pricing cattle at $68.00, steady with this week's active sales, feedlot sources said.

Packers lowered bids following a slide in beef prices on Wednesday, although the lower prices moved a lot of beef, sources noted. Increased slaughter this week expanded beef supplies, which packers were moving through the door at 'fire sale' prices, sources said.
Beef cut-out values Wednesday fell $0.83 to $1.07 per cwt, on sales of 323 fabricated loads, USDA reported.
Sales this week in the Panhandle area nearly cleaned out showlists, but there were still enough high-quality cattle left unsold that owners were trying to sell them at $68.00, feedyard sources said.
Kansas showlists reportedly had more cattle left than the Panhandle but many were said to be unfinished and could use extra days on feed, sources there said.
Cattle had been pulled ahead in anticipation of strong packer demand and in an attempt to keep feedlots current, they said.
